title: The Real Reason You Forget Why You Walked Into a Room
hook: Why do you instantly forget tasks when entering a new room?

narration.text: When you walk through a doorway, your brain often creates an 'event boundary'.
This boundary separates different memories and experiences.
It helps your mind organise information and switch contexts.
So, entering a new room can effectively 'reset' your short-term memory.
The old environment and its associated thoughts are compartmentalised.
This makes it harder to recall the original intention from the previous room.
It is a normal cognitive function, not a sign of memory issues.
Have you noticed this 'doorway effect' happening to you often?

description: Ever walked into a room and instantly forgotten why you went there? This common experience is known as the 'doorway effect' or 'event boundary'. Discover the fascinating reason behind this memory quirk and how your brain organises information.
topic: why you forget why you walked into a room
